strings.index.001:
Emili Godes was a versatile photographer whose work spanned artistic creation, industry,
        science, advertising and film. His eye brought photographic modernity into all these
        fields, from Barcelona and over more than five decades.
strings.index.005: Emili Godes working in his photographic laboratory, against a red background.
strings.biografia.001:
Emili Godes Hurtado (Barcelona, 1895–1970) was a versatile photographer whose career spanned more than five decades. He worked in industrial, advertising, scientific, medical, artistic and film photography, while also exploring the creative possibilities of the image.

His career reflects the transformation of photography during the twentieth century: from his early years of technical training to the adoption of the languages of modernity and the avant-gardes across all kinds of professional commissions.

Despite this extensive and varied output, Godes never set about building an archive of his own work. Unlike other contemporary photographers, who organised and preserved their collections, his work became dispersed among commissions, companies, publications and institutions. The absence of a personal archive helps explain why he remains little known in some circles today, and why much of his work has had to be reconstructed from collections held in different places.
strings.biografia.002:
Emili Godes was born in Barcelona on 14 April 1895, into a family connected with music and the arts. His father was a tenor at the Liceo and a choirmaster. Emili received musical training in singing and violin, and also developed an interest in painting and art books. This education helped shape a sensibility that he would later bring to photography.

At around the age of fifteen he began working as an apprentice at Casa Riba, one of Barcelona’s leading photographic establishments. There he came into contact with cameras, materials, laboratory processes and international technical publications.
strings.biografia.003: Godes Hurtado family, 1920. Emili is first from the right.
strings.biografia.004: Emili working in the laboratory at his home.
strings.biografia.005:
During the 1910s he consolidated his practical training. After Casa Riba he went on to work at Casa Cuyàs, where he became head of the laboratory. The experience gave him an in-depth knowledge of photographic processes and of the technical possibilities offered by new equipment.

During these years he also began submitting photographs to competitions and developing a body of personal work. From the outset, his professional activity coexisted with a desire for artistic experimentation: photography was not only a trade, but also a means of expression.
strings.biografia.007: Emili Godes and Antònia Diago with their children Montserrat and Jesús, 1924.
strings.biografia.008:
In 1928 he established himself as an independent photographer, although he had already undertaken commissions on his own account. In 1927 he had produced an extensive photo report on Córdoba, its streets and monuments, work that already shows his interest in architecture, the city and composition.

He also documented the urban development and construction works on Montjuïc associated with the 1929 Barcelona International Exposition. During the 1920s and 1930s he also worked on reproductions of works of art, industrial photography, advertising and photo reports for institutions and companies. His relationships with artists, galleries and specialist publications brought him closer to the modern currents of his time.

The Exposition also marked a turning point: from 1929 onwards his interest increasingly shifted towards technical and scientific photography. In the 1930s he was photography director of the journal Arxius de l’Escola Superior d’Agricultura and collaborated with the Chair of Entomology at the University of Barcelona.
strings.biografia.010: Urban development and construction works on Montjuïc.
strings.biografia.011:
During the Spanish Civil War he collaborated photographically with the Comissariat de Propaganda de la Generalitat de Catalunya.

In 1938, shortly before Nationalist troops reached Catalonia, he took part in the filming of Sierra de Teruel, the film André Malraux directed in Barcelona based on his novel L’Espoir. Filming, much of it carried out at the Orphea studios, was interrupted by the advance of the war, and the film could not be released until years later, in France and under the title L’Espoir.

After the Republican defeat, he destroyed some of his negatives to avoid possible reprisals and had to process the documentation required to continue working. The war and repression caused a rupture and partly explain the loss of material from that period, which today makes it more difficult to reconstruct his work.
strings.biografia.012: Advertisement in La Publicitat — Emili Godes Hurtado.
strings.biografia.013: Parets del Vallès during the war.
strings.biografia.014: French poster for Espoir · Sierra de Teruel, André Malraux’s film, on which Godes worked in 1938.
strings.biografia.015:
In the post-war period he rebuilt and expanded his activity and broadened his collaborations. He worked for companies, laboratories, scientific institutions and medical specialists, producing industrial and advertising photography for firms such as Catalana de Gas y Electricidad, Coca-Cola, Laboratorios Esteve, Myrurgia and Osram, among others.

His friendship with Francisco García del Cid, Dr Antoni Puigvert and the Escola Superior d’Agricultura brought him closer to scientific and medical photography, close-up photography and photomacrography. He also developed a significant activity as a stills photographer and made three short films: Màgica Nit, La Calumnia and Todo es según el color….
strings.biografia.016: The Godes Hurtado brothers (Josep, Ernest, Ramon, Emili and Artur) with Jesús Godes Diago, 1942.
strings.biografia.017: Montserrat Godes, Emili Godes and Antònia Diago, 1949.
strings.biografia.018:
During the 1950s and 1960s he continued working as a professional photographer for companies, scientists, doctors and film studios. He continued to process his negatives and prints personally in the laboratory installed at his home.

He was a professional capable of adapting to different clients, techniques and visual languages without abandoning his own way of seeing. He died in Barcelona on 20 February 1970, aged 74, while still working as a photographer.

strings.obra.001: Emili Godes’s work spans artistic creation, industry, science, advertising, film and the documentation of his time. Explore the archive by theme and decade, enter each project and open each photograph to view its record.
strings.destacadas.001: These photographs offer a journey through Emili Godes’s work: from urban landscapes and architectural images to scientific photography, industry, advertising, film and artistic experimentation. Together they show how the same eye could adapt to very different commissions and contexts without relinquishing precision, composition or modernity.
strings.destacadas.004: A selection of the most distinctive works in the Emili Godes archive.
strings.investigacion.001: This study approaches Emili Godes’s work through the presence of modernity and the photographic avant-gardes in his output. The research reconstructs aspects of his biography, locates little-known works and places his work within the photographic, artistic, technical and social context of Catalonia.

strings.investigacion.003: The research was carried out by Laia Foix as the final project for the Postgraduate Diploma in Management, Preservation and Dissemination of Photographic Archives at the Escuela Superior de Archivística y Gestión de Documentos. It corresponds to the 2013–2014 academic year and was published within the documentary environment of the Institut d’Estudis Fotogràfics de Catalunya.
strings.investigacion.004: It combines three lines of work: a bibliographic review, consultation of contemporary newspapers and magazines, and the location and study of photographs held by heritage institutions and private collections. It includes interviews with descendants, especially Maria Rosa Godes and Emili Godes Faura, and gives particular weight to primary sources.
strings.investigacion.005: To contextualise Godes’s production alongside that of his Catalan, Spanish and international contemporaries.
strings.investigacion.006: To complete his biography using family testimony, bibliography and primary sources.
strings.investigacion.007: To review and locate work dispersed among institutions, private collections and publications.
strings.investigacion.008: To advance the chronological dating and identification of his photographs, especially in less familiar fields (medical, scientific, industrial and advertising photography).
strings.investigacion.009: The study itself notes that the research remains open: there are still institutions to consult, bibliography to review, people to interview and photographs to identify. The texts and records on this website may combine several sources (final project, family records, institutional catalogues) and indicate when information is still awaiting confirmation.

strings.obra.intro.fotografia_artistica:
Art photography was a constant dimension of Emili Godes’s career. From his earliest work and competition entries to his Córdoba series, his images explore composition, atmosphere, light and photography’s capacity to construct a personal way of looking at the world.

This category includes only images conceived primarily as photographic creation, not every visually appealing photograph made as part of a professional commission.
strings.obra.intro.fotografia_industrial: Godes produced an extensive body of industrial work for companies and factories. His images document facilities, manufacturing processes, machinery, workers and products, but do more than record what is there: they organise space, study light and turn industry into an image of modernity and progress.
strings.obra.intro.publicidad: Advertising photography demanded clarity, precision and the ability to turn a product or service into an appealing image. Godes worked for a range of companies and applied to these commissions devices associated with modern photography: rigorous framing, contrasts, geometry and particular attention to lighting.
strings.obra.intro.ciencia_medicina: Godes’s relationships with scientists, doctors and research institutions led him to work with plants, insects, natural structures, operations and medical research. In these images, technical precision and documentary usefulness coexist with a strong visual dimension. His collaboration with Francisco García del Cid and the Escola Superior d’Agricultura was crucial.
strings.obra.intro.reproduccion_arte: Godes photographed paintings, sculptures, ceramics, jewellery and other works of art for artists, galleries, publications and catalogues. This activity required mastery of lighting, tonal reproduction, scale and fidelity to the original, and kept him in direct contact with the artistic production of his time.
strings.obra.intro.foto_fija_cine: From the 1930s onwards Godes worked as a stills photographer, mainly for the Orphea studios. He documented scenes, shoots, sets, actors and production materials. Research has identified his participation in more than fifty films.
strings.obra.intro.arquitectura_instalaciones: Architecture appears in many of his photo reports: buildings, factories, laboratories, scientific facilities, exhibition spaces and residences. Godes used the camera to explain how spaces are organised and how architecture can represent an idea of progress, efficiency or distinction.
strings.obra.intro.reportajes_urbanos_documental: The photo reports on Córdoba, Barcelona and other settings show Godes’s ability to observe cities, streets, monuments, activities and social transformations. They are documentary images, but also visual constructions in which perspective, light, scale and rhythm matter.
strings.obra.intro.experimentacion_fotografica: Godes explored double exposures, photograms, unconventional framing, contrasts, enlargements and close-up techniques. This category brings together images in which formal and technical investigation is the principal element.
strings.obra.intro.fotografia_familiar:
Godes also turned the camera towards his own family. These images portray the Godes family during the 1910s and 1920s: portraits of his daughter Montserrat, his siblings and his parents, first communions, weddings, outings to Montserrat, the snowfall of 1924 and everyday life in the family home on Carrer Bertran in Barcelona.

The group includes stereoscopic plates for the Taxiphote and, as well as forming a family album, became a testing ground where he experimented with framing, light and portraiture using the models closest to him.
